forum.title: CubeMX not generating timebase IRQ handler for different timebase source.
forum.best_answer_content:
Hello @JulioCalandrin

I have performed a test with the latest version of STM32CubeMX 6.17.0, and it is working as expected.

![GhofraneGSOURI_0-1778229618451.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/f4ae3c86-aac5-5eb9-dbb1-e0d669be4d8f.png "GhofraneGSOURI_0-1778229618451.png")

I highly recommend updating to the latest versions: STM32CubeMX 6.17.0 and STM32CubeIDE 2.1.1.

PS : STM32CubeMX 6.17.0 is no longer integrated into STM32CubeIDE 2.1.1. Instead, the two tools are now interoperable.

For more details , please check the following LINKs:

STM32CubeMX download Link:[STM32CubeMX | Software - STMicroelectronics](https://www.st.com/en/development-tools/stm32cubemx.html)

[STM32CubeIDE 2.0.0 workflow tutorial - STMicroelectronics Community](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus/stm32cubeide-2-0-0-workflow-tutorial/ta-p/864831)

[STM32CubeIDE 2.0 release - early heads-up! - STMicroelectronics Community](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-mcus/stm32cubeide-2-0-release-early-heads-up/td-p/810967)

THX

Ghofrane

scraped_replies.html:
I am able to consistently reproduce this issue on STM32CubeMX version 6.18.0 on Linux. Occasionally the generated code will contain the interrupt handler for the specified timebase source, but usually it doesn’t.

 

Details on my project in case they are relevant:

  • Part: STM32F413CHUx
  • Using freeRTOS
  • timebase source is TIM1 but I have also had the issue with TIM5 and TIM14
  • on the NVIC panel I have confirmed the “Time base: TIM1 update...” interrupt table row has “Generate Enable in Init”, "Generate IRQ handler”, and “Call HAL handler” checked

 

This a painful bug in STM32CubeMX because you must manually recreate the interrupt handler every time you generate code, otherwise your code will fail to run.
